label: ko marking an animate or definite object, and a recipient
note: ko is introduced by HI-C91-ko, and the note is exactly right that only the fused mujhe was present. The lesson takes aapko apart in front of the reader -- aap plus ko -- so the postposition is recovered from a word they already say rather than presented as new. It teaches both jobs the point names: the recipient (bacce ko, TO the child) and the marker a definite or human object wears (aadmi ko). The note's own observation is carried into the lesson, that this is the exact counterpart of the proxy's a before a human direct object, so the demand is not unique to Hindi and only the marker is.
